## 1. The capability you are building

Read a small Python program as tokens, expressions, statements, and blocks; identify what is syntactically valid before reasoning about behavior.

This is a connected learning sequence, not a reference list. In every lesson,
write a prediction, run the smallest complete example, explain the evidence,
make one controlled change, and retain one useful failure.

## 2. Before you start

**Prior knowledge:** Complete Unit 0 and bring its challenge notes and debugging record.

Prepare one notebook or project folder for the unit. Keep a four-column evidence
log: prediction, observed result, explanation, and next controlled change.

## 3. Lessons

| Step | Lesson | Purpose |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | [Values, Names, Expressions, and Statements](values-names-expressions-statements.qmd) | Build one part of the unit outcome through prediction, execution, explanation, modification, and debugging. |
| 2 | [Keywords, Operators, and Python's Vocabulary](keywords-operators-vocabulary.qmd) | Build one part of the unit outcome through prediction, execution, explanation, modification, and debugging. |
| 3 | [Indentation, Blocks, and Multiline Syntax](indentation-blocks-multiline.qmd) | Build one part of the unit outcome through prediction, execution, explanation, modification, and debugging. |
| 4 | [Comments, Introductory Docstrings, and Syntax Errors](comments-docstrings-syntax-errors.qmd) | Build one part of the unit outcome through prediction, execution, explanation, modification, and debugging. |
| 5 | [Unit Challenge](challenge.qmd) | Integrate the unit skills and preserve evidence from a clean rerun. |

## 4. How to study this unit

1. Attempt prediction prompts before executing code.
2. Type or adapt examples instead of only reading them.
3. Treat quiz errors as diagnoses and explain why each distractor fails.
4. Complete the challenge from a clean state and retain debugging evidence.

::: {.callout-tip title="Do not optimize for speed"}
The goal is not a fast first run. Aim to explain why the program behaved as it
did and how one controlled change produced new evidence.
:::

## 5. Unit evidence

By the end, retain working exercises, quiz corrections in your own words, one
debugging record, and a challenge solution that passes from a clean state.
